hexcasting.page.abandoned_greatwork.1: The ancients left behind, and those who come after follow. I am neither the first Hex Caster, nor will I be the last.$(br2)Across the world, ruins left by ancient Hex Casters are scattered about. Though abandoned and cast into the mundane world, these structures still reflect the glory and brilliance they once held as Greatworks.
hexcasting.page.abandoned_greatwork.2: It seems the Hex Casters of old also created a special material to test the skill of their apprentices. Those who passed the trial would receive a reward.$(br2)Unfortunately, my records on this are not yet detailed enough. I should conduct more in-depth research when the opportunity arises.

hexcasting.page.truth_crystal.1: One of the most fascinating relics left behind by ancient hexcasters is the $(l)Truth Crystal$(). These mysterious crystals appear to have been used as testing tools — designed to evaluate the skill of an apprentice by challenging them to produce specific spell patterns.
hexcasting.page.truth_crystal.2: A Truth Crystal contains a riddle: two sets of input lists, and two sets of expected output lists. The aspiring hexcaster must cast a spell that, when applied to the inputs, produces the correct outputs.$(br2)Each crystal also has a length limit that restricts how long the submitted pattern list may be.
hexcasting.page.truth_crystal.3: To attempt a riddle, place the Truth Crystal into a $(l)Truth Crystal Base$(), then right-click the base while holding an item containing a spell (such as a Cypher or Focus). The crystal will evaluate your spell and judge the result.
hexcasting.page.truth_crystal.4: If successful, the crystal will be consumed and a reward will be granted from a loot table specific to that crystal.$(br2)Crystals that were crafted by the player are marked as $(o)practice$() items — they can be tested without being consumed, but yield no reward upon success.
hexcasting.page.truth_crystal.crafting: The Truth Crystal Base is crafted by combining charged amethyst, slate, and amethyst dust.
